```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(framework)
scaffold()
```

Framework's cache stores R objects as files in `outputs/cache/` (gitignored)
with a record in `framework.db`. It's for results that are slow to compute
and safe to reuse, such as a fitted model. Run notebook 02 first: this one
reads `inputs.final.bp_long`.

```{r}
bp_long <- data_read("inputs.final.bp_long")
```

## Start clean

`cache_flush()` empties the cache, so the timings below show a real first run.

```{r}
cache_flush()
cache_list()
```

## cache_remember(): compute once, reuse after

The question for the tour: does systolic pressure change differently over the
visits in the two arms? A mixed model with a random intercept per participant
accounts for repeated visits. The `Sys.sleep()` stands in for a model that
takes a while.

```{r}
fit_bp_model <- function(data) {
  Sys.sleep(2)
  lme4::lmer(systolic_bp ~ visit_number * treatment + age + sex + (1 | participant_id), data = data)
}
```

The first call runs the expression and stores the result. Look at the elapsed
time.

```{r}
first_run <- system.time(
  bp_model <- cache_remember("bp_mixed_model", fit_bp_model(bp_long), expire_after = "1 day")
)
first_run["elapsed"]
```

The second call finds the cached model and returns almost at once.

```{r}
second_run <- system.time(
  bp_model <- cache_remember("bp_mixed_model", fit_bp_model(bp_long))
)
second_run["elapsed"]
```

The cached object is the full model. The `visit_number:treatmentintervention`
row is the difference in slope between arms, in mmHg per visit.

```{r}
round(summary(bp_model)$coefficients, 2)
```

`refresh = TRUE` forces a recompute, for example after the data changes.
`refresh` also takes a function, such as one that checks a file's timestamp.

```{r}
refresh_run <- system.time(
  bp_model <- cache_remember("bp_mixed_model", fit_bp_model(bp_long), refresh = TRUE)
)
refresh_run["elapsed"]
```

## cache() and cache_get(): store and fetch directly

`cache()` stores a value under a name, and `cache_get()` fetches it, or returns
`NULL` when it's missing or expired. Here, the per-arm counts of
participants by BP category at their first visit.

```{r}
baseline_categories <- bp_long |>
  filter(visit_number == 1) |>
  count(treatment, bp_category)

cache("baseline_bp_categories", baseline_categories)
cache_get("baseline_bp_categories")
```

Expiry takes hours as a number, or text such as `"30 minutes"`, `"12 hours"`,
`"2 days"`, or `"45 seconds"`. Look at `expire_at` for an entry kept 30
minutes.

```{r}
cache("site_list", db_query("SELECT site_name FROM sites", "study"), expire_after = "30 minutes")
cache_list()[, c("name", "expire_at", "created_at")]
```

This one expires after a second, so the `cache_get()` that follows finds
nothing.

```{r}
cache("short_lived_note", "check again tomorrow", expire_after = "1 second")
Sys.sleep(1.5)
cache_get("short_lived_note")
```

## cache_list()

Every entry, with when it expires and when it was last read. Entries with no
`expire_after` don't expire.

```{r}
cache_list()
list.files("outputs/cache")
```

## Forgetting and flushing

`cache_forget()` removes one entry and its file; `cache_flush()` removes all of
them.

```{r}
cache_forget("baseline_bp_categories")
cache_list()$name
```

```{r}
cache_flush()
cache_list()
list.files("outputs/cache")
```
